{{Quote|The divisions between the Faithful and the Faithless split every clan: members of the Ordos, Fetts, Kryzes, Awauds, Priests, Gedycs, and, yes, Vizslas, belonged to both sides in our struggle.|[[Tor Vizsla]]|<ref name="TBHC">''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''</ref>}}
'''Clan Gedyc''' was a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] clan. Following the rise of the peaceful [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorian]] faction in the aftermath of the [[Mandalorian Excision]], members of Clan Gedyc were divided in their support of the pacifist sect and the traditional [[Soldier/Legends|warrior]] clans.<ref name="TBHC" />

By [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], [[Lorka Gedyc]] had ascended to the head of [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]], a radical Mandalorian splinter faction<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> that dreamed of the return of the Mandalorians' ancient [[Mandalorian Crusaders|conqueror]] ways.<ref name="TBHC" /> Under Lorka Gedyc's leadership, [[Death/Legends|Death]] Watch allied with the newly-[[Declaration of a New Order|risen]] [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], aiding the Imperials' efforts to establish a [[Garrison/Legends|garrisoned]] [[City of Bone|presence]] on the Mandalorian [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]].<ref name="ImpCom501st" />

==Behind the scenes==
Clan Gedyc was first alluded to with the appearance of Lorka Gedyc in the novel ''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]'', written by [[Author/Legends|author]] [[Karen Traviss]] and published [[October 27]], [[2009]]. However, it was only with the [[2013]] release of the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] reference book, ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]'', that Clan Gedyc truly entered ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]].
